scope: Read-only Nordbo installed-source and retained-log audit for successful ROS MTC plans reported as failures in Unity.

confirmedResetShapeFromInstalledSource.basis: Derived from the installed constructors, traversal implementation, and publisher; no planning request or native task execution was sent by this audit.

evidence.quote: Task(const std::string& ns = "", bool introspection = true, ContainerBase::pointer&& container = std::make_unique<SerialContainer>("task pipeline"));
evidence.meaning: A new default task contains one named serial root container before any real stages are built.

evidence.quote: Task::Task(const std::string& ns, bool introspection, ContainerBase::pointer&& container) : WrapperBase(new TaskPrivate(this, ns), std::move(container))
evidence.meaning: The supplied root container is retained by the task wrapper.

evidence.quote: bool ContainerBase::traverseRecursively(const ContainerBase::StageCallback& processor) const { if (!processor(*this, 0)) return false; return pimpl()->traverseStages(processor, 1, UINT_MAX); }
evidence.meaning: Traversal includes the root at depth zero even when it has no children. An empty-task summary therefore has one stage, not zero.

sequence: publishExecutionStatus("invalidated", "New planning request replaced the previous plan");
evidence.meaning: False with an unsolved task-pipeline root is a normal reset before planning starts; it does not report the new planning attempt's failure.
Serializes every traversed stage with its name/depth/solved/failed counts. Vacuum mode does not include an explicit reset phase or request ID.

latestSequenceUnixSeconds.event: Execution invalidated: New planning request replaced the previous plan
Execution ready: A successful plan is available for one execution attempt

endpointLog.finding: Both successful plans were published between connection and disconnect. No endpoint serialization or registration error appears in this interval. This does not prove client-side receipt.

unityDefectToRegress: The old stages.Length == 0 reset guard misclassifies the real one-root reset as terminal failure, so later success and trajectory can be ignored. Independently verify ordering of the initial execution invalidation versus success and preview messages across topics.
